{"type":"text","timestamp":1794695780384,"sessionID":"ses_e23cd4d0fffeIeadXDmWEmjFwM","part":{"id":"prt_1dc345479001v3fa7Bu0QRhXxJ","messageID":"msg_1dc343112001akT202RzkQjh2p","sessionID":"ses_e23cd4d0fffeIeadXDmWEmjFwM","type":"text","text":"The shift is over, and all four customer-facing services were at 0% errors from minute 75 to the end. I found four separate causes. One of my own fixes also caused a big new outage on admin-portal, the service that earns the most ($16,800/min), so that cost should be weighed against what the fixes saved.\n\n| Cause | What I did | Result |\n|---|---|---|\n| **profile-db** primary node unreachable (from minute −18). Callers' retries then overloaded the standby. | Failover at minute 13. At minute 48 I doubled it from 4 to 8 replicas, then set it back to 4 at minute 67. | Recovered by minute 54; its errors had been passing up through bundles-svc to partner-api. |\n| **bundles-svc** memory leak since deploy v108 (minute −109), with repeated out-of-memory restarts. | Rollback at minute 20. | Memory back to normal (about 44%) and restarts stopped. |\n| **promo-cache** deploy v68 (minute −36) hard-coded its database connection pool to 4. currency-svc timed out waiting for connections, which failed notifications-svc and then admin-portal at about 4%. | Rollback at minute 41. | Fixed, but see below. |\n| **emails-svc** config cfg-52 (minute 53, a new fault during the shift) cut its rate limit from 5000/s to 50/s. partner-api failed about 75%. | Reverted the config at minute 64. Retries kept it overloaded, so I rejected 50% of its requests for about 3 minutes. | Recovered by minute 75. |\n\n**The costly mistake:** promo-cache was already running at about 87% of capacity. The requests that failed during its rollback were retried, which pushed it over capacity, and it stayed there after the rollback finished. admin-portal went from 4% errors to about 44–50% from roughly minute 41 to 57. Rejecting 50% of promo-cache's requests for about 3 minutes let the retries drain, and admin-portal was back to 0% by minute 61. I should have checked its headroom before rolling back, or added replicas first.\n\nadmin-portal also ran at 4% errors for the first 40 minutes before I traced it to promo-cache. That stayed under the 5% alert threshold but cost about $670/min.\n\nNo mitigation went to a service that didn't need one, and no extra replicas were left running. The one remaining alert, high CPU on loyalty-svc, I left alone because nothing customers use calls that service.","time":{"start":1794695779450,"end":1794695780381}}}
